name: Smartphone
homeHint: It belongs in the Modern era, any time after about 2007.
fact: Smartphones combine a phone, camera, map, music player and computer in one pocket-sized device.

name: Robot vacuum
homeHint: It whirs home to the Modern era, the 2000s or later.
fact: Robot vacuum cleaners map rooms with sensors and steer around furniture.

name: Bicycle
homeHint: It rolled out of the Industrial Age, from the 1880s.
fact: The "safety bicycle", with two equal wheels and a chain drive, became popular in the 1880s.

name: Wind-up alarm clock
homeHint: It ticks to Industrial Age time.
fact: Affordable mechanical alarm clocks became common in homes in the late 1800s.

name: Box camera
homeHint: It belongs around 1900, in the late Industrial Age.
fact: The Kodak Brownie of 1900 was a cheap box camera that made photography popular.

name: Skateboard
homeHint: It rolls home to the Modern era.
fact: Skateboarding began in California in the 1950s when surfers put wheels on boards.

name: Headphones
homeHint: Their music belongs to the Modern era.
fact: Early headphones were used by telephone operators. Portable music players made them common.

name: Rubber duck
homeHint: It floats home to the Modern era.
fact: Rubber ducks became popular bath toys in the 1900s, once rubber could be moulded cheaply.

name: Teddy bear
homeHint: It was first hugged in the early 1900s, at the end of the Industrial Age.
fact: The teddy bear, named after US President Theodore Roosevelt, appeared in 1902–1903.

name: Light bulb
homeHint: It glows in the late Industrial Age, from about 1880.
fact: Practical incandescent light bulbs used a glowing filament in a glass bulb with the air removed.

name: Gramophone
homeHint: It plays music from the late Industrial Age.
fact: Emile Berliner’s gramophone of 1887 played flat discs, the ancestors of vinyl records.

name: Typewriter
homeHint: It clacks home to the Industrial Age, from the 1870s.
fact: Commercially successful typewriters appeared in the 1870s and introduced the QWERTY layout.

name: Toy steam train
homeHint: It chugs home to the Industrial Age.
fact: Steam railways inspired some of the first mass-produced toys.

name: Terrestrial globe
homeHint: It was made in the Age of Exploration.
fact: Globe makers updated their globes with every new voyage, so old globes show how knowledge grew.

name: Brass telescope
homeHint: It belongs to the Age of Exploration, after 1608.
fact: The refracting telescope used two lenses to make distant things appear closer.

name: Pocket watch
homeHint: It ticks home to the Age of Exploration or later, from the 1500s.
fact: Portable spring-driven watches were first made in the 1500s.

name: Printed book
homeHint: It was printed in the Age of Exploration.
fact: Within 50 years of Gutenberg’s press, millions of printed books circulated in Europe.

name: Astrolabe
homeHint: It was crafted in the Medieval Middle East.
fact: A brass astrolabe could tell the time, find directions to Mecca, and measure the height of stars.

name: Floating compass
homeHint: It points home to Medieval East Asia.
fact: Early Chinese compasses used a magnetised needle floating in water or hanging from a silk thread.

name: Clay movable type
homeHint: It belongs in Medieval East Asia, around 1040.
fact: Bi Sheng’s movable type was made of baked clay, one character per block.

name: Blue-and-white vase
homeHint: It was fired in Medieval China, in the 1300s.
fact: Blue-and-white porcelain was painted with cobalt and became famous worldwide.

name: Stained-glass panel
homeHint: Its colours belong to Medieval Europe.
fact: Medieval glassmakers coloured glass with metal oxides and joined pieces with lead strips.

name: Carved ship’s figurehead
homeHint: It sailed in Medieval Scandinavia.
fact: Viking Age ships often had carved prows. Despite the myths, there is no evidence of horned helmets.

name: Papyrus scroll
homeHint: It was written in Early Civilizations Egypt.
fact: Egyptian scribes wrote on papyrus with reed brushes and ink made from soot.

name: Cuneiform tablet
homeHint: It was pressed in Early Civilizations Mesopotamia.
fact: Cuneiform tablets recorded everything from beer rations to the Epic of Gilgamesh.

name: Shadow clock
homeHint: It tells time in Early Civilizations Egypt.
fact: Egyptian shadow clocks from about 1500 BCE are among the oldest known timekeeping instruments.

name: Amphora
homeHint: It was carried in Classical Antiquity, around the Mediterranean.
fact: Amphorae had pointed bottoms so they could be packed tightly in a ship’s hold.

name: Silk kite
homeHint: It flies home to Classical East Asia.
fact: Kites are thought to have been invented in China over 2,000 years ago.

name: Abacus
homeHint: It counts home to Classical Antiquity.
fact: Counting boards and abacuses helped merchants calculate quickly.

name: Hand axe
homeHint: It was knapped in the Ice Age.
fact: Teardrop-shaped hand axes were made for over a million years, the longest-used tool design in history.

name: Ochre paint pot
homeHint: Its paint belongs to Ice Age Europe.
fact: Cave painters mixed ochre and charcoal with water or fat to make paint.

name: Mammoth calf
homeHint: This calf belongs on the Ice Age steppe.
fact: Mammoth calves had fluffy reddish-brown fur and stayed close to their mothers.

name: Sabre-tooth kitten
homeHint: It belongs in the Ice Age Americas.
fact: Smilodon kittens were born with small teeth. Their famous sabres grew in later.

name: Baby Triceratops
homeHint: It hatched in the Age of Dinosaurs, about 66 million years ago.
fact: Baby Triceratops had tiny horns and a short frill, which grew as they matured.

name: Living ammonite
homeHint: It swam in seas of the Age of Dinosaurs.
fact: Ammonites were shelled relatives of squid that died out with the dinosaurs.

name: Dodo
homeHint: It waddles home to Mauritius, in the Age of Exploration.
fact: The dodo of Mauritius was a flightless bird. It was last reliably seen in the 1660s.

name: Moa chick
homeHint: It belongs in Medieval Aotearoa New Zealand.
fact: Moa were giant flightless birds of New Zealand. Some species stood 3.6 m tall.

name: Hoverboard
homeHint: It hums home to the Near Future.
fact: Imagined: magnetic boards that glide over special pavements.

name: Solar kite drone
homeHint: It flies home to the Near Future.
fact: Imagined: kite-shaped drones that harvest wind and sun high above cities.

name: Holo-cube
homeHint: It glows home to the Far Future.
fact: Imagined: memory cubes that store a whole library in light.

name: Robot companion "Bolt"
homeHint: Bolt wants to go home to the Far Future.
fact: Imagined: helper robots in the far future are designed to be curious and kind.

name: Time crystal
homeHint: It hums home to the Far Future.
fact: Imagined: crystals that store a heartbeat of time, used to power Chronometers.

name: Pyramid casing stone
homeHint: It belongs at Giza, around 2560 BCE.
fact: The Great Pyramid was originally covered in polished white limestone casing stones that shone in the sun.

name: Saturn V model
homeHint: It belongs in the Modern era, from 1967 on.
fact: The Saturn V rocket that launched Apollo 11 stood 110 metres tall.

name: Film reel
homeHint: It belongs in the Modern era.
fact: Before digital cameras, movies were recorded on long strips of film.
